hints: Focus on the class of each alcohol first, as primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols behave very differently toward oxidation.
X is primary, Y is secondary and Z is tertiary, so think carefully about which of these can be oxidised by mild reagents like acidified dichromate.
For dehydration, draw the alkene formed from Y as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and check if each C of the double bond has two different groups for cis-trans isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Classify X, Y and Z**

Look at the carbon bearing the $\text{OH}$ group and count how many other carbons it is joined to.

X = $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is primary (1 other C). Y = $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is secondary (2 other Cs). Z = $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is tertiary (3 other Cs).

**Decide who is oxidised**

Remember the simple rule: primary to aldehyde then acid, secondary to ketone, tertiary resists oxidation.

Mild oxidising agent (e.g. $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}^+$):
$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$
So only X and Y react.

**Dehydrate to an alkene C5H10**

Dehydration removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give an alkene. For cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism, each C of $\text{C=C}$ must have two different groups.

Y (pentan-3-ol) dehydrates to pent-2-ene:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This alkene exists as cis and trans forms.

**Check X and Z do not give cis-trans**

X (pentan-1-ol) gives mainly pent-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which has two H atoms on C1, so no cis-trans.

Z gives mainly 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CHCH}_3$, which has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups on one C of the double bond, so no cis-trans. Therefore Y only is correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it claims all three react with mild oxidising agents. Z is a tertiary alcohol, $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2CH_3$, and has no H on the C-OH carbon, so it resists mild oxidation. This is a common trap if you forget the classification rule.
options.B: Incorrect on both columns. Like A, it wrongly includes tertiary alcohol Z as oxidisable. It also wrongly says Z gives cis-trans isomers, but Z gives $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$ which cannot show cis-trans because one end has two identical methyl groups.
options.C: Correct on both counts. Only X (primary) and Y (secondary) are oxidised, Z (tertiary) is not. Only Y dehydrates to pent-2-ene, $CH_3CH=CHCH_2CH_3$, where each double-bond carbon carries two different groups, giving a cis-trans pair.
options.D: Half right but half wrong. It correctly identifies X and Y only for oxidation, but wrongly assigns the cis-trans alkenes to Z only. Z gives branched alkenes with no E/Z isomerism, while Y gives pent-2-ene which does.
